transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I have a hard time sitting still. Like in staff meetings, or those church event briefings, I feel like there’s a motor running under my skin. I end up shifting around, standing up, or finding some reason to move.
Do you feel this way only in meetings or events, or do you also notice it happening in other places, like at home or when you’re out with friends?

It’s not just meetings, no. It’s mostly when I’m expected to sit still anywhere… staff meetings, church briefings, that kind of thing. I get this restless feeling, like something’s humming under my skin, and I end up shifting around or finding a reason to stand up or move.
Do you also feel this restlessness during other times, like when you're relaxing at home or trying to unwind?

Yeah… I mean, even at home I don’t really just sit down. After work I’ll end up in the garage, messing with tools or sorting things again. And on my shifts I’m kind of always moving from one thing to the next—mopping, trash, chairs… I don’t stop much.

So you mentioned feeling restless both at work and at home — how about in other situations, like when you're out with friends or trying to relax and watch a movie? Do you still feel that same need to keep moving or stay busy?

Yeah… I do. Even when it’s supposed to be relaxing, like fishing with my wife, I’m messing with the tackle box or fidgeting with something. Or at bingo, I’ll tap the pencil, talk a little too loud… stuff like that. It’s hard for me to just sit quiet and enjoy it.
When did you first start feeling this way? Was it something you noticed as a kid, or did it come on more recently?

It goes back pretty far, I guess. Grade school, really. I used to get in trouble for getting out of my seat, talking over the teacher… rushing ahead before they finished directions. My mom would say I was wound too tight, even then.
